knowledge:
- key_parameters: dat=A list of data frames containing feature-level test results (columns: mz, time, p-value, F-statistics) ;; type=A list of strings specifying the ion mode for each data frame in dat (e.g., "pos", "neg") ;; pa=Pathway information database summarized from Mummichog and SMPDB ;; hmdbCompMZ=Pre-processed database of common adduct ions and HMDB IDs ;; pos.adductlist=Character vector specifying the allowed adducts for positive mode ;; neg.adductlist=Character vector specifying the allowed adducts for negative mode ;; p.threshold=P-value threshold to determine which metabolic features are considered significant ;; n.permu=Number of permutations to perform when use.fgsea is FALSE ;; fractional.count.power=Power term (p) to tune the penalty for multiple-mapped features ;; max.match.count=The maximum cap for multiple-matching count (m) to limit the penalty ;; use.fgsea=Logical; if TRUE, conducts GSEA-type testing; if FALSE, conducts permutation testing ;; use.meta=Logical; when use.fgsea is TRUE, controls whether testing is metabolite-based (TRUE) or feature-based (FALSE)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when conducting pathway enrichment analysis on untargeted metabolomics data from positive mode, negative mode, or both, and you need to account for metabolite-feature matching uncertainties.
- pitfalls: Multiple-matching of features to metabolites can bias results if not penalized; use fractional.count.power and max.match.count to control this. Ensure that the input data frames contain at least the three required columns: m/z, retention time, and feature p-value.

workflows.name: metapone_pathway_analysis
workflows.intent: Conduct metabolic pathway testing from untargeted metabolomics feature-level test results using permutation or GSEA-type testing.
input: pos_features.csv (positive mode feature-level test results containing m/z, retention time, and p-value)
neg_features.csv (negative mode feature-level test results containing m/z, retention time, and p-value)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the metapone package and input feature-level test results ;; 2. Load the built-in HMDB compound m/z mapping and pathway databases ;; 3. Define the allowed adduct lists for positive and negative modes ;; 4. Run the pathway testing using the metapone function ;; 5. Extract and filter significant pathways using ptable and ftable ;; 6. Visualize the pathway testing results using bbplot1d and bbplot2d
workflows.code:
library(metapone)
data(pos)
head(pos)
data(neg)
head(neg)
data(hmdbCompMZ)
head(hmdbCompMZ)
data(pa)
head(pa)
pos.adductlist = c("M+H", "M+NH4", "M+Na", "M+ACN+H", "M+ACN+Na", "M+2ACN+H", "2M+H", "2M+Na", "2M+ACN+H")
neg.adductlist = c("M-H", "M-2H", "M-2H+Na", "M-2H+K", "M-2H+NH4", "M-H2O-H", "M-H+Cl", "M+Cl", "M+2Cl")
dat <- list(pos, neg)
type <- list("pos", "neg")
r<-metapone(dat, type, pa, hmdbCompMZ=hmdbCompMZ, pos.adductlist=pos.adductlist, neg.adductlist=neg.adductlist, p.threshold=0.05,n.permu=200,fractional.count.power=0.5, max.match.count=10, use.fgsea = FALSE)
#r<-metapone(dat, type, pa, hmdbCompMZ=hmdbCompMZ, pos.adductlist=pos.adductlist, neg.adductlist=neg.adductlist, p.threshold=0.05,n.permu=100,fractional.count.power=0.5, max.match.count=10, use.fgsea = TRUE, use.meta = TRUE)
#r<-metapone(dat, type, pa, hmdbCompMZ=hmdbCompMZ, pos.adductlist=pos.adductlist, neg.adductlist=neg.adductlist, p.threshold=0.05,n.permu=100,fractional.count.power=0.5, max.match.count=10, use.fgsea = TRUE, use.meta = FALSE)
hist(ptable(r)[,1])
selection<-which(ptable(r)[,1]<0.025)
ptable(r)[selection,]
ftable(r)[which(ptable(r)[,1]<0.025 & ptable(r)[,2]>=2)]
bbplot1d(r@test.result, 0.025)
bbplot2d(r@test.result, 0.025)
